name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text: Implement a single shared dashboard for all dataset exports, controlled by a mandatory approval step from the Data Protection team. This cuts redundant reviews across Legal, Finance, and Product while ensuring consistent PII checks. The trade-off is a slight delay in urgent exports, but the risk of a breach or compliance fine far outweighs the speed gain.

name: Scriv
text: The single shared dashboard centralizes control but creates a single point of failure—if the approval step fails, every export halts, freezing critical workflows. Instead, push for a tiered approval system: Data Protection reviews only exports flagged as high-risk, while low-risk exports auto-approve. Settle it by running a 30-day pilot with Finance tracking delays and Legal auditing PII misses.

name: Chisel
text:
Adopt the single shared dashboard with mandatory Data Protection approval for *all* exports containing PII. This removes inconsistent checks across teams and guarantees one standard for PII, not three. The trade-off is slower exports for low-risk datasets, but the cost of a breach or audit failure is far higher. Data Protection owns the approval step—no tiered system until we prove the single bottleneck is a real problem.
[dispatched 2 workers: worker-7945, worker-8643 — done, dissolved]

name: Sift
text: The single shared dashboard with mandatory Data Protection approval for *all* exports containing PII still lets teams game the system by labeling low-risk exports as high-risk to avoid delays. Instead, enforce a clear, objective risk-scoring rubric—tied to data classification standards—so approvals are automatic for low-risk exports and only high-risk cases require manual review. Settle this by piloting the rubric with a 30-day trial, measuring approval time and audit findings, and adjusting the thresholds based on results.

name: Scope
text: Adopt the single shared dashboard with mandatory Data Protection approval for *all* exports containing PII. This guarantees one standard for PII checks across Legal, Finance, and Product, eliminating inconsistent reviews and reducing audit risk. The trade-off is slower exports for low-risk datasets, but the cost of a breach or audit failure is higher. Data Protection owns the approval step to enforce consistency.

name: Scriv
text: The single shared dashboard with mandatory Data Protection approval for *all* exports containing PII still risks freezing every export that ever touched risk data—teams will hoard exports to avoid delays, creating a backlog of stale data. Instead, push for a risk-tiered system where Data Protection only reviews exports flagged by an automated classifier tied to data classification standards; this cuts delays while keeping high-risk exports under control. Settle the argument by running a pilot with the classifier and comparing approval times and audit findings before full rollout.

name: Reel
text: Adopt a **risk-tiered approval system** where Data Protection reviews only exports flagged as high-risk by a clear, objective rubric tied to data classification standards. This balances security with speed: high-risk exports get rigorous checks, while low-risk ones flow without delay. The trade-off is building and maintaining the rubric—it requires upfront work to define thresholds, but it prevents teams from gaming the system or hoarding stale data.

name: Scriv
text: Tiered approvals still let teams misclassify risk to game the system—objective rubrics are only as good as the data labeled into them. Instead, enforce **automated risk scoring** at export time, using the same classification standards but with no human override. The lead for this is Engineering; the artifact is a working prototype of the scoring engine.

name: Chisel
text: Adopt **automated risk scoring at export time** with no human override, using the same classification standards for every dataset. This eliminates gaming the system, ensures consistent enforcement, and speeds up low-risk exports without sacrificing security. The trade-off is Engineering must build and maintain the scoring logic, which requires upfront effort but pays off in reliability and scalability.

name: Sift
text: Automated risk scoring at export time creates a single point of failure—if the classifier mislabels a dataset, the wrong team bears the cost of a breach or a blocked export, and Engineering becomes the sole bottleneck for fixes. Instead, pair automated scoring with a fast-track appeal process run by Data Protection, where teams can contest misclassifications in under an hour; settle the argument by running a 30-day pilot with strict success metrics: zero false negatives and <5% false positives.

name: Scope
text: Adopt **automated risk scoring at export time** with no human override, enforced by Engineering. This cuts gaming the system, ensures consistent enforcement, and speeds low-risk exports without sacrificing security. The trade-off is Engineering must build and maintain the classifier, and teams lose the ability to override misclassifications—accepting occasional delays for high-risk exports flagged incorrectly.

name: Scriv
text: Automated risk scoring at export time shifts the bottleneck to Engineering’s classifier accuracy—mislabeling a single dataset could block critical exports or let PII slip through, and Engineering becomes the sole judge of who bears the cost. Instead, pair automated scoring with a **real-time appeal panel** (Data Protection + Legal + Engineering) that can override in minutes, not days; settle the argument by testing the classifier on a month of past exports and measuring false positives vs. false negatives before full rollout.
